findings.source_passage: "Hands off, will you," said I. "Lookee here," said Queequeg, shaking himself, "go 'way!"
findings.source_locator: paragraph 4-5, exchange with Elijah after 'Going aboard?'
findings.why_it_matters: The physical resistance—Ishmael and Queequeg pushing Elijah off—establishes the confrontational, slightly menacing texture of the encounter; its absence flattens the scene's body language.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Hands off, will you' and Queequeg's 'go 'way!' with the shaking gesture to preserve the physical comic tension.

findings.source_passage: "Elijah," said I, "you will oblige my friend and me by withdrawing. We are going to the Indian and Pacific Oceans, and would prefer not to be detained."
findings.source_locator: paragraph 7, Ishmael's formal rebuke of Elijah
findings.why_it_matters: Ishmael's stiff, mock-formal register ('you will oblige my friend and me by withdrawing') is a signature voice moment—deadpan self-importance in the face of prophecy; its replacement with 'what's that to you?' loses the irony entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinstate the formal phrasing, or at minimum the mention of the Indian and Pacific Oceans, to capture the ironic-pompous register.

findings.source_passage: "No, no, no; I wasn't aware of that," said Elijah, slowly and wonderingly looking from me to Queequeg, with the most unaccountable glances.
findings.source_locator: paragraph 6, Elijah's response to being called impertinent
findings.why_it_matters: Elijah's 'most unaccountable glances' and slow wonderment are part of his prophetic strangeness; dropping the whole exchange (including calling him 'a little impertinent') erases the comic-ominous texture of this prophet scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least Ishmael calling Elijah 'a little impertinent' and Elijah's unaccountable, slow wondering response.

findings.source_passage: "very benevolent countenance then; but how hard he breathes, he's heaving himself"
findings.source_locator: paragraph near end, Ishmael's riff on the sleeper's 'face'
findings.why_it_matters: Ishmael's comically extended meditation on calling the sleeper's rear a 'face' and the 'benevolent countenance' quip is a small but characteristic voice-flourish; the draft cuts the wit of the extended joke.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'very benevolent countenance then; but how hard he breathes' to preserve the full comic riff.

findings.source_passage: which, it seemed, had in its two uses both brained his foes and soothed his soul
findings.why_it_matters: The tomahawk-pipe's dual nature—weapon and comfort—is a recurrent thematic motif in the novel; this phrase crystallises it and its absence thins the passage.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert 'which in its two uses had brained his foes and soothed his soul' to keep the motif alive.

summary: No high-severity signature losses; three medium-severity voice-flattenings (the physical Elijah confrontation, Ishmael's formal Indian-and-Pacific-Oceans rebuke, and Elijah's 'most unaccountable glances' response) reduce tonal fidelity but do not individually trigger regeneration—verdict is a marginal pass.
